choices.content: Central symmetry is a relationship between two figures, while being centrally symmetric is a property of a single figure.
The two terms have exactly the same meaning, with no difference.
A centrally symmetric figure is a figure that coincides with itself after a \(90^\circ\) rotation about a point.

question.prompt: Which of the following statements about “central symmetry” and “centrally symmetric figures” is correct?

solutions.explanation: Central symmetry describes two figures that coincide with each other after a \(180^\circ\) rotation about a point. A centrally symmetric figure coincides with itself after a \(180^\circ\) rotation about a point.
solutions.title: Compare the two definitions
